Germany for growing up. Ireland for living and working. Incredible what a German upbringing can do to your work morale combined with Irish expectations.

Most people in Germany do 'mini jobs' meaning they only work enough hours to make 450 euros a month. I'm one of the few people who asked to work for 30 hours a week, and I also have a couple other part time jobs on top of that. I'm not orignally from Germany either.

6No, not most people. There are people that do mini jobs, but that is very far from "most people". Students do it, stay at home mums do it, pensioners do it. That is about it.

Regulary, you will do your 40 hours + whatever it takes to get the requested work done, which often times leads to unpaid overtime. If you only knew people that worked mini-jobs, you probably were a student or in a very fucking low income & employment area. Likely in eastern Germany.

Edit: And before you call me a fag, I lived and worked there for about 30 years, I have friends still living there.

I'm in my early 30s and it seems like everyone I know, as well as roommates and random co-workers, are all about the Minijobs... I do live in East Germany though, and while it's less expensive than living in North America, I haven't had issues finding work even though my German sucks.

Yeah, in Eastern Germany you get that. That is because unemployment is rampant there. Go to any other part of Germany and you will see a wildly different picture. People will work 40+ hours usually and very few people will have mini jobs. I actually don't know anybody that is considered "employed" that is working a mini-job, but times are bad in the east. Last night I talked to a friend that works long hours and has 100k/year and another one that has 80k. And they both work their assess off.
Maybe I came from a place that really sucked, but I love it here and don't think things are bad at all!
My brother moved to the east and he loves it too. I didn't mean to put you down for it, but your claim that most Germans work mini-jobs was just very wrong.

This probably seems really, really stupid, but how does one become a moderator for sub voats? It wouldn't hurt to explain to me like I'm five.
Message the mods in a subverse and ask if they need a mod. Alternatively, post on /v/modsforhire
Create your own subverse, send a private message to one of the mods of an existing subverse or if they haven't been active for 2+ months then request that sub in /v/subverserequest.

There are multiple options.

Start a subverse about a topic that you are interested in and build it from the ground up. Be sure to add some content before publishing it on /v/newsubverses. This way people can see what the verse has to offer and might contribute or even subscribe.

Second option is contacting a mod of a already established sub of your liking and offer to help. Be sure to tell them what you have to offer and what your plans are to increase traffic or the general quality of the sub.
